summary: Stevens County lookout tower dated to 1938 (1934 newspaper items hint earlier), removed or toppled in 1954; footings and ruins remain on the summit.

facts.design: 30-foot pole tower with an L-4 style cab
facts.status_note: The tower came down in 1954; ruins and footings remain on the summit.

access.note: Reached on foot by a route of about 2 miles one way; no closure is described in the sources. Level inferred from the route descriptions, not verified with the Forest Service.

visit.trail_note: WillhiteWeb lists a 2-mile one-way hike with about 1,000 ft of gain by the north route, from Highway 20 up South Fork Mill Creek Road.

events.note: A Colville Examiner item describes a crew finishing work at the lookout tower in August 1934; CCC men ran a telephone line up to the station that September.
Register, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb give 1938 for a 30-foot pole L-4 tower; WillhiteWeb says the date is unclear given the 1934 reports.
The lookout man moved into the station in mid-July 1938.
Register says removed; WillhiteWeb says toppled; firelookout.com says destroyed. Ruins remain on the summit.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb give 1938, but a 1934 newspaper describes a crew still finishing work at the lookout tower. Not resolved; the story gives both.
The register says removed in 1954, firelookout.com says destroyed, WillhiteWeb says toppled. All agree the tower was gone after 1954.

sources.title: Green Mountain, Forest Lookouts (Washington), quoting The Colville Examiner

notes_for_editor: Build date unresolved: 1938 in three sources, 1934 newspaper references to a finished or finishing tower. Staffing and fate rest on one register and two lookout-history sites. Access level 'public' is inferred from route descriptions with no closure noted; verify with Colville NF before publishing. Do not confuse with the Green Mountain Lookout near Darrington in Snohomish County (us-wa-green-mountain), a separate standing lookout. The brief's status 'gone' and kind 'tower' are supported.
